messages:
Alex P: Hey team — seeing AccessDenied on kms:Decrypt when our ingestion lambda (assumed-role: ingest-runner) tries to decrypt envelope keys after a recent key rotation. Error snippet: 
```
AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/ingest-runner/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:222222222222:key/abcd-1234
```
Alex P: We didn't change role perms; suspect key policy or grant behavior after rotation. Anyone seen this pattern? :thinking_face:
Priya S: quick checklist — does the role have kms:Decrypt in its IAM policy? is the KMS key policy restrictive to principals? are you relying on grants? any session policies when calling AssumeRole?
Alex P: IAM role has `kms:Decrypt` allowed. Key policy is fairly locked down, only the management account + a few roles. We used a rotate that created a new key and pointed the alias. No explicit grants that I know of.
Ben G: if alias moved to a new key, ciphertexts encrypted with old key should still decrypt by old key, but if something used a grant token during encrypt/decrypt and it's missing you can get AccessDenied. also if assume-role call had `SessionPolicy` or `Tags` conditions, KMS evaluates them.
Alex P: here's the assume-role call we use in the lambda exec (simplified):
```
sts:AssumeRole
RoleArn: arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/ingest-runner
SessionTags: {project:airflow}
```
Priya S: important: key policy can include conditions on `aws:PrincipalTag` or `kms:EncryptionContext:...`. If the key policy expects a tag on the principal (e.g., `StringEquals "aws:PrincipalTag/project": "airflow"`) make sure the session tags are passed and validated by STS. Also if you added a session policy that removes kms:Decrypt it can block.
Alex P: the key policy does have a condition on `aws:PrincipalTag/project` — it was added to tighten cross-account access. We thought session tags would propagate. But still failing.
Ben G: two debugging commands to try from a debug runner that can assume the same role:
```
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/ingest-runner --role-session-name debug --duration-seconds 900 --tags Key=project,Value=airflow --debug
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://edk.bin --grant-tokens "<optional-grant-token>" --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:222222222222:key/abcd-1234 --region us-west-2
```
Priya S: also check CloudTrail for KMS events — `Decrypt` calls include `principalIdentity` and whether a `GrantToken` was supplied. If grant-based, you need the GrantToken from the encryptor side to be presented during decrypt. Grants are ephemeral and tied to the key version.
sec-bot: doc: KMS cross-account access with session tags — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/grants.html (linked)
Alex P: ran the assume-role with `--tags` and then the aws kms decrypt from that session. Still got AccessDenied. CloudTrail shows Decrypt request `principalId` as the assumed-role session and the requestContext shows no grant token. No GrantId in logs.
Ben G: Could be that the key policy condition checks for `aws:PrincipalArn` or `aws:SourceAccount` instead of tags. Paste the key policy snippet?
Alex P: pasted snippet:
```
{
  "Sid": "AllowIngestWithTag",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/ingest-runner"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:PrincipalTag/project": "airflow"}}
}
```
Priya S: aha — small gotcha: when a role is assumed, session tags are only copied into the principal's tag set if you allowed `sts:TagSession` and the caller had permission to pass tags. The role's trust policy also needs `sts:TagSession`? Actually the caller must have `sts:TagSession` in the permissions and the trust relationship must allow `sts:AssumeRole` with `sts:TagSession`. Double-check that the caller that performs AssumeRole is passing tags and not being stripped by an inline session policy.
Ben G: also check whether tags are actually visible to KMS: sometimes there's a delay or you have to set `aws:PrincipalTag` vs `aws:RequestTag` nuance. Another thing: if the principal in key policy is the role ARN (not the assumed-role principal), KMS evaluates `aws:PrincipalTag` on the request principal (the session), not the role resource. So you need the session to have tag.
Alex P: we were assuming tags propagated automatically. The caller that does AssumeRole is the lambda itself (it re-assumes via an intermediate cross-account role). That intermediate step wasn't passing tags. Found it — the pipeline's job that does the assume didn't forward tags when calling STS -> session had no `project=airflow` tag.
Priya S: nice find. Solution paths: 1) update the pipeline to pass tags through all assume-role hops and ensure caller has `sts:TagSession` permissions; 2) relax key policy to accept the role ARN without tag for this particular action (less preferred); 3) create a grant for the role (grants don't need session tags but are bounded in time and must be used with grant token if immediate).
Alex P: we patched the pipeline to forward tags and added `sts:TagSession` to the deploy role. Re-ran and decrypt succeeded. Confirmed in CloudTrail: Decrypt now shows the session with `project=airflow` in principal tags. :thumbsup:
Ben G: follow-up — consider adding an automated test to assume-role with tags and call kms:Decrypt after future rotations to catch regressions.
Infra Deploy Bot: created issue #512 in infra-checks: "AssumeRole tag propagation test" and scheduled nightly smoke test.
Alex P: thanks all — leaving the key policy as-is for safety. Will document the multi-hop tag propagation caveat in our onboarding doc.
